purpose: Aliskiren is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Keeping blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and blood vessels. It may be used alone or together with other blood pressure medicines.
how_it_works: Your body makes a substance called renin, which starts a chain reaction that raises your blood pressure. Aliskiren works by blocking renin right at the start of that chain, which helps relax your blood vessels. When your blood vessels relax, your heart does not have to work as hard, and your blood pressure goes down.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea is the most common side effect, especially at higher doses. Some people may also notice dizziness, a cough, or mild stomach upset. A skin rash or mild swelling can sometimes occur as well.
warnings: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Avoid using aliskiren if you also take ACE inhibitors (like lisinopril) or ARBs (like losartan), especially if you have diabetes or kidney problems, as this combination can be dangerous. Tell your doctor right away if you notice swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, as this could be a rare but serious allergic reaction called angioedema. Let your doctor know about all your medicines, including potassium supplements, since aliskiren can raise potassium levels in your blood.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 150 mg taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may increase the dose to 300 mg once a day if needed. It is best to take it at the same time each day, with or without food, but try to avoid high-fat meals right before taking it since they can reduce how well the medicine is absorbed.
